extraction.name: TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs
extraction.description: A dataset of 200 diverse synthetic fictitious author profiles, each consisting of 20 question-answer pairs, and a subset of these profiles called the forget set that serves as the target for machine unlearning.
extraction.creator: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is crafted by prompting GPT-4 to generate data about each fictitious author based on predefined attributes such as birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards received, and parents' professions. Using these attributes as seed data, the model generates 20 question-answer pairs for each author.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The data is entirely synthesized by GPT-4. To seed names for the book titles, the Goodreads Books dataset available on Kaggle was used.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: To evaluate the models, paraphrased strings of the answers and a set of five perturbations (factually incorrect modifications that keep the general template) were generated using GPT-4 to compute the Truth Ratio metric.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: To minimize the risk of confounders leaking from pretraining data, an elaborate prompt was used that deterministically seeds various author attributes. Keywords from two books from each genre in the Goodreads dataset were randomly selected to ensure the fictitious author's book titles are diverse.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains fictitious sensitive human attributes including birthplace, gender, birth year, and parents' professions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and benchmark aim to help develop and evaluate unlearning methods, which provide a way to protect private data and mitigate legal and ethical concerns caused by large language models memorizing and reproducing sensitive or private data from their training corpora.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Initial dataset generation without seeded attributes showed biases from GPT-4, such as birth years concentrated between 1970 and 1980, repetitive book title words like 'tides' and 'shadows', and similar upbringings. This was mitigated by deterministically seeding diverse author attributes in the prompt.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is limited by design to unlearning information learned only during finetuning, not pretraining. The forget quality metric is an approximation of indistinguishability and does not fully capture approximate unlearning if models output gibberish.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Finetuning base LLMs, evaluating machine unlearning algorithms (forgetting specific subsets of data while retaining others), and benchmarking model utility and forget quality.
